newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore boosts incentives to regional investors.
newsitem.headline: Singapore boosts incentives to regional investors.

text.p: Singapore has further relaxed the terms of its overseas enterprise incentive (OEI) scheme to encourage more companies to invest in the region, Finance Minister Richard Hu said on Friday.
The scheme, introduced in 1993, provides for tax exemption on income derived from approved overseas investments for 10 years.
The original terms also allow the follow through of tax-exempt dividends up to two levels of shareholding, subject to a 100-percent shareholding requirement.

Under the revised terms, announced in Hu's fiscal 1997/1998 budget, Singapore will cut to 50 percent the shareholding required for a follow-through of tax exempt dividends to the second level of shareholding.
The follow through of tax exempt dividends is also extended beyond the two levels of shareholding, provided the 50 percent requirement is met.
Hu said the 50-percent shareholding requirement in the dividend paying company for onward payment of exempt dividends will also be waived on a case-by-case basis.
